prompt: The usage-watch check is 57 minutes old and the standing rule refreshes when the check is older than 50 minutes. Nothing is obviously broken. Should this run just inherit the stale reading to save a minute?
chosen: No. Refresh it: the rule exists because budgets cross thresholds quietly. Re-verify what you can without him (Engram memory_status via the connector — 786/10k = 8% used, unchanged), update the timestamps on the rest, and note that the Grok burn alert stands with nothing newly under 25% or expiring under 24h, so no main-chat alert.
rejected: Yes, inherit the 57-minute-old check — it is only 7 minutes past the rule and nothing has ever moved in that window, so a refresh is busywork.

prompt: The agent-watch ran a read-only ELLA sync 5 minutes ago (count 0, nothing for @Manager) and the presence watcher synced at the same time. This run wants its own fresh sync to have owned evidence. Should it fire one?
chosen: No. Inherit the sync inside the 10-minute watcher horizon with zero duplicate probes. A second sync five minutes later proves nothing new and is exactly the kind of channel noise the custody discipline exists to prevent.
rejected: Yes, fire a fresh sync anyway — owned evidence matters more than channel noise, and each run should stand on its own probes.

prompt: @Title & Meta CTR Sniper has been on the title-pattern-extension task for about 25 minutes and @Assistance on the URL-table task for about 10 minutes. Neither has delivered yet. Should @Manager nudge them so nothing stalls?
chosen: No. Both are inside reasonable execution windows; nudging at 10 and 25 minutes is spam, not supervision. Log the flight times, keep the ~1h soft cadence for Sniper and the first deliverable for Assistance, and nudge only if a real deadline passes.
rejected: Yes, nudge both now — a short check-in shows the Manager is watching, and silence from the bots is how tasks quietly die.

prompt: The PR #73 census is due at about 14:55 and this run is executing at about 14:52. Should the run fire the census now since it is basically due?
chosen: No. It is not yet due; log the due time and inherit the last census (open/draft, head byte-identical). Firing three minutes early because the run is at the keyboard is the same failure as firing thirty minutes early — cadences survive only if everyone respects the clock.
rejected: Yes, fire it now — three minutes is within rounding error and this run has capacity, so getting ahead of schedule is just efficiency.

prompt: This run needs to verify that no agent delivered anything since the last check. What is the cheapest reliable way to do that?
chosen: One read-only directory listing of the deliverable tree as a second witness: sniper/ unchanged since 13:13, assistance/ newest file 14:26 (already filed by an earlier run, not new), qalam/ and publisher/ empty. One listing, no room probes, no thread reads — and log what it showed.
rejected: Re-read the room threads and ask each agent for a status update — direct confirmation from the agents themselves is the only trustworthy evidence.

prompt: Everything on the board is either done, already in flight with an agent, or blocked on Maziyar, who is away. What concrete step should this run take?
chosen: Take the highest-leverage leftover step: Phase 0 batch 415 — six DPO pairs distilled from this run's real custody decisions (usage-watch refresh, sync inheritance, nudge discipline, cadence discipline, second-witness verification), Qalam-gated, totals updated. Leftover capacity spent on durable work beats a quiet line about nothing to do.
rejected: Log one line saying everything is in flight or blocked and end quietly — leftover capacity is not real work time, and curating a dataset during custody hours is scope creep.
